pixelObservations: Baohua is the larger rear/upper-half hall, not the smaller foreground gate.
Main silhouette is one-storey, single-eave, broad ridged roof with hipped-gable form and upswept corners. Roof shows yellow/ochre glazed ridges over dark/weathered valleys.
Facade has dark-red/brown timber and joinery; central doorway is flanked by two grille-window bays; low pale gray stone base is visible.
The slender paired poles stand in the forecourt and align with official flagpole description. Do not treat them as evidence of a deep porch.
Rear/north projection is not actually exposed in this frontal elevated photo. Its existence is text-supported; exact roof geometry/joins remain unseen.
Foreground gate, nearby enclosure walls, courtyard censer and vegetation are context, not part of the hall body.
